grammar[0].blocks[1].blocks[1].text: mit *mir*, bei *dir*, von *ihm*, zu *ihr*: after aus, bei, mit, nach, seit, von, zu — always these forms.
grammar[0].fact: German sizes are not English sizes: a UK 12 is about a German 40, and shoes go by a different scale altogether. The assistant will ask *Welche Größe haben Sie?* and expect a number you don’t know.

grammar[1].subheading: Four verbs for shops and tables, where the person comes in the dative
grammar[1].blocks[0].title: The thing does it to you
grammar[1].blocks[0].note: The thing is the one who does it, and you get it: *Der Mantel gefällt mir*, not *ich gefalle*. In the plural: Die Schuhe *gefallen* mir.
grammar[1].blocks[1].title: I like it: three ways
grammar[1].blocks[1].text: *Das gefällt mir*: I like how it looks or sounds. *Das schmeckt mir*: I like how it tastes. *Ich mag das*: I like it in general. And *Ich liebe dich* is only for people you mean it about.
grammar[1].blocks[2].title: In the shop
grammar[1].blocks[2].note: *Ich schaue nur*: I’m just looking. It works in every shop.
grammar[1].blocks[3].title: Words for the practice page
grammar[1].fact: Shops in Germany have no legal duty to take back what you simply don’t like, unless you bought it online. Most big stores do anyway, if you keep the receipt: ask *Kann ich das umtauschen?*

opener.caption: Im KaDeWe in Berlin: nicht nur Kleider. Ganz oben gibt es Essen.
reading.intro: Max has a wedding on Saturday and nothing to wear, so Lena takes him to the big department store in Berlin. The assistant has been there for thirty years and has one sentence.
reading.photos[0].caption: Das KaDeWe zu Weihnachten: Hier steht auch der Baum sehr gut.
reading.photos[1].caption: Diese Schuhe? Sie stehen Ihnen sehr gut.
reading.en: Verkäufer: Hello! Can I help you? · Max: Yes, please. I need a suit. Do you like this one, Lena? · Lena: I don’t like that one. It’s brown. You’re not a sofa. · Verkäufer: Do try it on. Oh! That suits you very well. · Max: The trousers are too short. They don’t fit me. · Verkäufer: They suit you very well. Short is modern. · Lena: Take the blue one. I like it better. · Max: The blue one is too big! I look like a child in it. · Verkäufer: That suits you very well. · Lena looks at the assistant. She takes the curtain off the changing room and hands it to Max. · Lena: Max, put that on. · Verkäufer: Oh! That suits you very well. The colour goes with your eyes. · Max: Really? How much is it? · Lena: Max. · Max: What? I like it. And I’ll be the only one at the wedding with a curtain.
reading.fact: Berlin’s KaDeWe opened in 1907 and is one of the largest department stores in Europe. Its sixth floor is a food hall with more cheeses than most people will meet in their lives, and many visitors never get as far as the clothes.
reading.tasks[1].instruction: Complete with mir, dir or Ihnen, as in the text.
document.caption: Vor dem Geschäft: Prozente!
document.intro: A real sign outside a clothes shop. *Markenqualitäten* are brand-name goods, and *reduziert* means reduced. It is short, because it does not need to say much: the % does the talking.
document.fact: Germany had a law until 2004 that allowed big sales only twice a year: the *Sommerschlussverkauf* and the *Winterschlussverkauf*. The law is gone, but people still say *SSV* and *WSV*, and queue as if it weren’t.
document.tasks[1].instruction: Everything is half price. Write the new price.
document.tasks[2].instruction: Answer the assistant, with mir or Ihnen.
